by North Forty News Staff | NorthFortyNews.com

As Northern Colorado residents prepare for the holiday shopping season, artificial intelligence is making it increasingly difficult to distinguish legitimate online bargains from sophisticated scams.

Fraudsters are using AI-generated product images, convincing advertisements, fabricated customer reviews, and realistic-looking retail websites to trick consumers into sharing financial information or purchasing products that never arrive.

According to the Federal Trade Commission, shopping scams were the most frequently reported type of scam originating on social media in 2025.

Credit Union of Colorado, which serves members in Fort Collins, Greeley, and communities throughout the state, is encouraging shoppers to recognize warning signs and take additional precautions before making online purchases.

“Scammers have always relied on trust, urgency,y and emotion, but artificial intelligence is making their tactics even more convincing,” said Chelsey Bogacz, director of risk management at Credit Union of Colorado. “A professional-looking website, realistic advertisement,t or familiar brand name doesn’t necessarily mean an offer is legitimate. We encourage consumers to slow down, verify who they’re dealing with, and be cautious about sharing personal or financial information before making a purchase.”

Holiday promotions often feature substantial discounts, limited-time offers, and advertisements designed to encourage quick purchases. Those same tactics can make fraudulent offers appear legitimate.

Fake online stores can closely imitate established businesses, copying logos, product photographs,s and website designs.
